question_text: Show that the points (5,4,2), (6,2,−1), (8,−2,−7) are collinear.

mark_split.label: Add two of them to get the third

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you compute, and what relation between the three proves collinearity.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the three distances
steps.margin_note: First mark. Take the three points in pairs and apply the distance formula, which in three dimensions carries a third squared difference. Leave every answer in surd form.
steps.memory_tip: Three pairs, three distances, each with a third squared difference. Keep them as surds.

recall.must_convey: That the three pairwise distances AB, BC and AC are computed with the 3D distance formula.
accept: compute all three distances with the three dimensional distance formula
root of x difference squared plus y difference squared plus z difference squared
find A B, B C and A C
apply the distance formula three times

steps.why: Both questions on this page are answered by computing the SAME three distances. Only the conclusion drawn from them differs, which is why the book prints the note 'Questioning is different but Answering is similar' underneath.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the third squared difference and using the 2D formula.
Simplifying a surd wrongly, which hides the pattern in the three answers.

steps.label: Add two of them to get the third
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Three points are collinear exactly when the two SHORTER distances add to the longest — the middle point then lies on the segment joining the other two.
steps.memory_tip: √14 + 2√14 = 3√14, so the two shorter add to the longest and the points are collinear.

recall.must_convey: That two of the distances add to the third, so the points are collinear.
accept: two of the distances add up to the third so the points are collinear
the shorter two sum to the longest
since they add exactly the points lie on one line
rendu kalipithe moodavadi vasthundi kabatti collinear

steps.why: If the three points were NOT in a line they would form a triangle, and in any triangle two sides are strictly GREATER than the third. Exact equality is what rules a triangle out.
common_mistakes: Adding the wrong two distances — the longest must be the sum, not an addend.
Concluding collinear from an approximate rather than exact match.

insider_note: All three distances reduce to multiples of √14, and the longest, AC = 3√14, is the one that must equal the sum of the other two. Leave the surds unsimplified and the match cannot be seen.
